correctness.rationale: A cyclic-image map kills G′ and is specified by its quotient functional and a generator of its image; idempotence means that the map fixes this generator. Normalizing the nonzero quotient line yields λ(u)=1 and a unique generator h above u for that map. Every element of the coset above u has order p and gives a legitimate lift, with exactly p^c choices; no centrality is used. The word ‘central-fiber’ in the proof is inessential and should be understood as an ordinary coset fiber. Equal nontrivial composites would force the same image and hence PQ=Q and QP=P, impossible for distinct maps. Thus adjacency is exactly the two cross-annihilations, giving an independent blow-up. Vertex and degree counts follow by fixing one or two independent functional values. In a clique the image vectors and functionals are biorthogonal, and independent image lines can be chosen in order and the dual coordinates extended freely in p^{k(d−k)} ways. Lifts and division by k! give the stated count. Extending by a basis of the common kernel gives maximal cliques of size d. In d=2 each base vertex has exactly one complement. In d≥3 choose r in ker λ outside span(u,v) (the kernel has dimension ≥2 and excludes u), and choose ρ with ρ(r)=1 and ρ(u)=ρ(v)=0. The intersection ker ρ∩ker μ is nonzero and meets span(r,v) only at zero, furnishing the second intermediary and distance at most three. In d≥4 ker λ∩ker μ contains a line outside span(u,v), producing a common neighbor; same-image distinct projections give nonadjacent pairs even without fibers. In d=3 the explicit pair has common kernel line ⟨e₁+e₂⟩ inside its image span, precluding a common neighbor for every p, including p=2. The component diameters for d=2 are 1 or 2 according to fiber size. Independent replay: python /workspace/replay/checks.py 4 composes the actual maps of an exponent-three Heisenberg group and enumerates complete clique counts by actual composition in F₂⁴ [1,120,1680,3360,840,0]; neither calculation substitutes for the group theorem.

Once the new group identification is proved, clique counts are multiplied by p^{ck}; distances between different fibers equal base distances, and distinct vertices in one fiber have distance two whenever the base degree is positive.

Neither base geometry nor its clique recurrence demonstrates that every lift in each coset is an idempotent retraction vertex with complete or empty cross-fiber adjacency. The proof uses cyclic-image factorization, exponent p on each nontrivial quotient coset, and equality of nontrivial composites forcing equal maps.

originality.rationale: The underlying abelian graph is the established nonincident point–hyperplane graph, not a new linear commuting graph. Several of its invariants are known or follow from prior local structure. The verified distinct claim is the exact uniform independent-fiber transfer for all finite prime-exponent groups, with the resulting counts and distance behavior for the actual retractions, irrespective of whether G′ is central. The inspected linear results do not provide that group transfer; the cited group comparisons concern particular families, not that full domain.

value.rationale: This solves a natural group-endomorphism graph problem on the entire finite prime-exponent class: the actual commutation relation, not only an endomorphism census, loses all multiplication-law information beyond the two quotient sizes. Exact clique and distance invariants make the transfer usable, including for noncentral derived subgroups; no new claim is needed for known projective counts in the abelian base case.
